reader.notes: Behaviour conforms. Diagnostic lead (misleads-diagnosis, minor): `RD R1 GLOBAL IS GLOBAL` is refused citing §1985:XIII.3.5.2, the Report Writer RD format, which has no GLOBAL clause; at 1985 the GLOBAL clause's format is §1985:X.4.4.2 (this rule's point). Site ReportSectionBinder.cs#BindReportDescriptionClauses, the UnrepeatedElements.AtMostOnce call for 'the GLOBAL clause'; repro E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/reread-1985-moved/out/work-1985-m03/src/rdglobref.cob.

refuter.evidence: The 1985 RD format (§1985:X.4.4.2) prints [ IS GLOBAL ] as its own clause beside CODE, CONTROL and PAGE, and §1985:XIII.3.5.3 SR2 makes their order immaterial. rdg2.cob (single program, RD R1 CONTROL IS FINAL PAGE LIMIT IS 20 LINES FIRST DETAIL 3 GLOBAL): --std 85 EXIT 0, 'LC=03': GLOBAL written last, after the whole PAGE clause, is accepted and the PAGE clause's FIRST DETAIL 3 governs the first detail line (Report Writer semantics kept); GLOBAL in a program that contains no other program is harmless. rdg1.cob (GLOBAL written INSIDE the PAGE clause, between LINES and FIRST DETAIL): EXIT 65, 'rdg1.cob(14,12): error COBOL0001: unexpected 'FIRST'': correctly refused, since GLOBAL is a clause of the entry and not a phrase of PAGE. The reader's rdglob (GLOBAL between CODE and PAGE in a contained program) and rdglobref (GLOBAL twice refused) stand. The reader's diagnostic lead (the repeated-GLOBAL message cites §1985:XIII.3.5.2, whose format has no GLOBAL clause) remains a misleads-diagnosis nit, not a behaviour failure. Citations: OK §1985:X.4.4.4 GR2 ('All other clauses in the report description entry are presented in the Report Writer module'); OK §1985:XIII.3.5.3 SR2 ('The order of appearance of the clauses following report-name-1 is immaterial').
